label: Own political scheme success
summary: Adds a flat amount to the success chance of political schemes the character runs.
details: Going by its name, it counts only schemes the character owns (starts), not schemes against them. It works on a character. The game documents nothing more.

label: Own political scheme growth
summary: Adds a flat amount to how fast the success chance of the character's own political schemes grows.
details: Going by its name, it affects the growth of the chance over time, not the chance itself. It works on a character. The game documents nothing more.

label: Own political scheme max success
summary: Adds a flat amount to the highest success chance the character's own political schemes can reach.
details: Going by its name, it raises the cap of the chance, not the chance itself. It works on a character. The game documents nothing more.

label: Own scheme secrecy
summary: Adds a flat amount of secrecy (how likely a scheme stays undetected) to the schemes the character runs.
details: The game's display name is "Scheme Secrecy". It works on a character. A negative value would make their schemes easier to discover.

label: Personal scheme speed
summary: Adds a flat amount to the phase duration of the character's personal schemes.
details: The game shows it as "Personal Scheme Speed". A scheme phase length is counted in days (the game's concept text) and a lower length makes a scheme progress faster, so a negative value speeds personal schemes up. It works on a character.

label: Personal tenet slots
summary: Adds a flat number of personal tenet slots for the character.
details: The game shows it as "Personal Tenets". A personal tenet is a core tenet that a ruler adopts as a part of their own spirituality. It works on a character.

label: Piety level impact
summary: Changes by a percentage how strongly the character's piety level affects them.
details: The game shows it as "Level of Devotion Impact". The piety level ("Level of Devotion") is the tier the character's piety places them in. This modifier scales up or down the effects they get from that level. It works on a character.

label: Piety rewards
summary: Changes by a percentage the piety the character gets as standalone rewards.
details: The game shows it as "Piety Rewards". "Standalone" is in the key; the game does not say which gains count as standalone. It works on a character.

label: Piety loss
summary: Changes by a percentage the piety the character loses in standalone losses.
details: The game shows it as "Piety Loss". The game does not say which losses count as standalone. A negative value would reduce such losses. It works on a character.

label: Player heir opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's player heir has of them (direction is a best reading).
details: The player heir is the heir a player keeps playing as when the ruler dies; usually the primary heir. The game shows the modifier as "Player Heir Opinion" and does not say whose opinion of whom; going by the other opinion modifiers, it is the heir's opinion of the holder. It works on a character.

label: Political scheme speed
summary: Adds a flat amount to the phase duration of the character's political schemes.
details: The game shows it as "Political Scheme Speed". A scheme phase length is counted in days (the game's concept text) and a lower length makes a scheme progress faster, so a negative value speeds political schemes up. It works on a character.

label: Inherit good traits chance
summary: Changes the chance of a child inheriting good congenital traits (hidden "inactive" ones, going by the key).
details: The game shows it as "Chance of inheriting good congenital traits". Congenital traits are traits that offspring can inherit. The word "inactive" in the key suggests traits the parent carries without showing; the game does not say so. It works on a character.

label: New good traits chance
summary: Changes the chance of a child getting a new good congenital trait.
details: The game shows it as "Chance of new good congenital traits". Congenital traits are traits that offspring can inherit. The game does not say how "new" is decided. It works on a character.

label: Powerful vassal opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's powerful vassals have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Powerful Vassal Opinion". Powerful vassals are the few vassals with the most soldiers and highest income; they expect a council seat. It works on a character.

label: Prestige level impact
summary: Changes by a percentage how strongly the character's prestige level affects them.
details: The game shows it as "Level of Fame Impact". The prestige level ("Level of Fame") is the tier the character's prestige places them in. This modifier scales up or down the effects they get from that level. It works on a character.

label: Prestige rewards
summary: Changes by a percentage the prestige the character gets as standalone rewards.
details: The game shows it as "Prestige Rewards". The game does not say which gains count as standalone. It works on a character.

label: Prestige loss
summary: Changes by a percentage the prestige the character loses in standalone losses.
details: The game shows it as "Prestige Loss". The game does not say which losses count as standalone. A negative value would reduce such losses. It works on a character.

label: Prisoner opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's prisoners have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Prisoner Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Provisions capacity
summary: Adds a flat amount to how many provisions (army supplies) the character's armies can carry.
details: The game shows it as "Provisions Capacity". Provisions are the food, water and shelter a camp can provide. It works on a character and on a terrain type.

label: Provisions capacity (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage how many provisions (army supplies) armies can carry.
details: It uses the same display name as provisions_capacity_add, "Provisions Capacity". It works on a character and on a terrain type.

label: Provisions gain
summary: Changes by a percentage how many provisions (army supplies) armies gain.
details: The game shows it as "Provisions Gain". It works on a character and on a terrain type. The game does not spell out when the gain happens.

label: Provisions loss
summary: Changes by a percentage how many provisions (army supplies) armies lose.
details: The game shows it as "Provisions Loss". A negative value would reduce the loss. It works on a character and on a terrain type. The game does not spell out when the loss happens.

label: Provisions use
summary: Changes by a percentage how many provisions (army supplies) armies use up.
details: The game shows it as "Provisions Use". A negative value would make armies use fewer. It works on a character, on a province and on a county.

label: Prowess
summary: Adds a flat amount to the character's prowess (their skill in personal combat).
details: A negative value lowers it. It works on a character. The game's note on prowess_no_portrait (it "doesn't affect portraits") implies that this plain version does change the portrait.

label: Prowess (percent)
summary: Changes the character's prowess (their skill in personal combat) by a percentage.
details: It uses the same display name as prowess, "Prowess". It works on a character.

label: Prowess (no portrait)
summary: Adds a flat amount to the character's prowess without changing how their portrait looks.
details: The game's own note: it does not affect portraits. The game also warns of odd results when you use negative values on people who have negate_prowess_penalty_add. It works on a character.

label: Prowess per influence level
summary: Adds prowess to the character for each influence level they have.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess per influence level". The amount is per level, so it grows with the level. The game documents nothing more. It works on a character.

label: Prowess per merit level
summary: Adds prowess to the character for each merit level they have.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess per merit level". The amount is per level, so it grows with the level. The game documents nothing more. It works on a character.

label: Prowess per piety level
summary: Adds prowess to the character for each piety level they have.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess per piety level". The amount is per level, so it grows with the level. The game documents nothing more. It works on a character.

label: Prowess per prestige level
summary: Adds prowess to the character for each prestige level they have.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess per prestige level". The amount is per level, so it grows with the level. The game documents nothing more. It works on a character.

label: Prowess per stress level
summary: Adds prowess to the character for each stress level they have.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess per stress level". Use a negative value to make stress cost prowess. The game documents nothing more. It works on a character.

label: Prowess scheme speed
summary: Changes the phase duration of schemes depending on the character's prowess.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess Scheme Speed". Going by the name, the character's prowess feeds into how long a scheme phase lasts. The game documents nothing about the formula or the unit. Its display text in the game files has a broken icon tag (`[prowess_i]` without `|E`).

label: Prowess scheme resistance
summary: Gives the character scheme resistance (a slowdown of schemes against them) based on their prowess.
details: The game shows it as "Prowess Scheme Resistance". Scheme resistance slows down schemes against the character. How prowess is turned into resistance is not documented. It works on a character.

label: Pursue efficiency
summary: Changes how effective the character's armies are at pursuing a retreating enemy.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it concerns the pursuit phase of battles. It works on a character and on a terrain type.

label: Raid speed
summary: Changes how fast the character's armies raid.
details: The game shows it as "Raid Speed" and marks it as a command modifier (a modifier of an army commander). The game documents no unit. It works on a character.

label: Realm priest opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's realm priest has of them.
details: The game shows it as "Realm Priest Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Head of faith opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the head of the character's faith has of them.
details: The game shows it as "Head of Faith Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Religious vassal opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's religious vassals have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Religious Vassal Opinion". The game does not define which vassals count as religious. It works on a character.

label: Retreat losses
summary: Changes the losses the character's armies suffer when they retreat.
details: The game shows it as "Retreat Losses" and marks it as a command modifier (a modifier of an army commander). A negative value would reduce the losses. It works on a character and on a terrain type.

label: Siege progress vs revolts
summary: Adds a flat amount to the siege progress the character's armies make against rebels (revolts).
details: The game shows it as "Siege Progress against Revolts". Siege progress shows how close a siege is to completion. It works on a character.

label: Siege progress vs revolts (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the siege progress the character's armies make against rebels (revolts).
details: It uses the same display name as revolting_siege_morale_loss_add, "Siege Progress against Revolts". Siege progress shows how close a siege is to completion. It works on a character.

label: Rite creation cost
summary: Adds a flat amount to the piety cost of creating or reforming a rite.
details: The game shows it as "Rite Creation and Reformation Cost". Going by the key, the cost is paid in piety. A negative value makes it cheaper. It works on a character.

label: Rite creation cost (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the piety cost of creating or reforming a rite.
details: It uses the same display name as rite_creation_piety_cost_add, "Rite Creation and Reformation Cost". A negative value makes it cheaper. It works on a character.

label: Same-culture holy order hire cost
summary: Adds a flat amount to the cost of hiring a military holy order of the same culture.
details: The game shows it as "Same-Culture Military Holy Order Hire Cost". A negative value makes it cheaper. Which culture it is matched against comes from the name ("same culture", presumably the character's own); the game does not say. It works on a character.

label: Same-culture holy order hire cost (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the cost of hiring a military holy order of the same culture.
details: It uses the same display name as the _add version. A negative value makes it cheaper. Which culture it is matched against comes from the name ("same culture", presumably the character's own); the game does not say. It works on a character.

label: Same-culture mercenary hire cost
summary: Adds a flat amount to the cost of hiring mercenaries of the same culture.
details: The game shows it as "Same Culture Mercenary Hire Cost". A negative value makes it cheaper. Which culture it is matched against comes from the name ("same culture", presumably the character's own); the game does not say. It works on a character.

label: Same-culture mercenary hire cost (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the cost of hiring mercenaries of the same culture.
details: It uses the same display name as the _add version. A negative value makes it cheaper. Which culture it is matched against comes from the name ("same culture", presumably the character's own); the game does not say. It works on a character.

label: Same culture opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that people of the character's own culture have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Same Culture Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Same faith, other rite: county opinion
summary: Adds a flat amount to county opinion of the character in counties whose faith is the same but whose rite differs.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it is about counties that share the character's faith but follow another rite. It works on a character and on a county.

label: Same faith, other rite opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that people of the character's faith who follow a different rite have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Same Faith, Different Rite Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Same faith opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that people of the character's own faith have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Same Faith Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Same heritage county advantage
summary: Adds a flat amount of advantage in counties that share the character's culture heritage.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it concerns counties of the same heritage as the character. It works on a character. The game documents nothing about what the advantage is used for.

label: Same rite county opinion
summary: Adds a flat amount to county opinion of the character in counties that follow the same rite.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it is about counties that follow the character's rite. It works on a character and on a county.

label: Same rite opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that people who follow the same rite as the character have of them.
details: The game shows it as "Same Rite Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Scheme discovery chance
summary: Changes by a percentage the chance that schemes are discovered.
details: The game shows it as "Scheme Discovery Chance". The game does not say whose schemes are meant (the character's own or ones against them). It works on a character.

label: Scheme speed
summary: Changes the length of a scheme's phases, in days.
details: The game shows it as "Scheme Speed". A lower phase length makes the scheme progress faster. It works on a scheme, so it is given by things attached to a scheme.

label: Scheme speed against a relation
summary: Adds to the phase duration of the character's schemes against people who have a given scripted relation to them.
details: `$SCRIPTED_RELATION$` stands for the key of a scripted relation, so each relation gives its own modifier; `rival` is a scripted relation in the base game, giving `scheme_phase_duration_against_rival_add`. The game gives no display name. It works on a character.

label: Scheme resistance
summary: Changes the scheme resistance applied to a scheme.
details: The game shows it as "Scheme Resistance". Scheme resistance slows schemes down: it is subtracted from the scheme owner's scheme speed. It works on a scheme; whether the value is a number of days is not stated.

label: Scheme secrecy
summary: Changes the secrecy (how well hidden it is) of a scheme.
details: The game shows it as "Secrecy". Secrecy decides how likely a hostile scheme stays undetected by its target. It works on a scheme. A negative value would make it easier to discover.

label: Scheme success chance
summary: Changes the success chance of a scheme.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it changes the chance itself. It works on a scheme.

label: Scheme success growth
summary: Changes how fast the success chance of a scheme grows.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it changes the growth of the chance over time. It works on a scheme.

label: Scheme max success chance
summary: Changes the highest success chance a scheme can reach.
details: The game gives no display name or description. Going by its name, it changes the cap of the chance. It works on a scheme.

label: Short reign duration
summary: Changes by a percentage how long the short reign effect lasts for the character.
details: The game shows it as "Short Reign Duration". Short reign is a decaying opinion penalty that characters in a realm get towards a new liege. Going by the name, this scales how long it lasts. It works on a character.

label: Daily siege progress
summary: Changes the siege progress the character's armies make each day.
details: The game shows it as "Daily Siege Progress" and marks it as a command modifier (a modifier of an army commander). It works on a character.

label: Siege phase time
summary: Changes the time a phase of a siege takes.
details: The game shows it as "Siege Phase Time" and marks it as a command modifier (a modifier of an army commander). A negative value would shorten phases. It works on a character and on a province.

label: Spouse opinion
summary: Adds to the opinion that the character's spouse has of them.
details: The game shows it as "Spouse Opinion". It works on a character.

label: Stationed regiment damage
summary: Adds a flat amount of damage to stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier (an example built from the pattern: `stationed_<type>_damage_add`). The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment damage (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the damage of stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment pursuit
summary: Adds a flat amount of pursuit to stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. Pursuit makes a victorious army turn more routed soldiers into dead ones after a battle. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment pursuit (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the pursuit of stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment screen
summary: Adds a flat amount of screen to stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. Screen reduces the casualties a defeated army takes after a battle. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment screen (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the screen of stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment siege value
summary: Adds a flat amount of siege value to stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game does not explain siege value; going by the name it is the unit's contribution to sieges. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment siege value (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the siege value of stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment toughness
summary: Adds a flat amount of toughness to stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. Toughness is how much damage a soldier takes in battle before becoming a casualty. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed regiment toughness (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the toughness of stationed men-at-arms of one type in the province.
details: `$MEN_AT_ARMS_TYPE$` stands for the key of a men-at-arms type, so each type gives its own modifier. The game gives no display name. It works on a province.

label: Stationed men-at-arms damage
summary: Adds a flat amount of damage to all stationed men-at-arms in the province.
details: The game shows it as "Stationed Men-at-Arms Damage". Unlike the type-specific versions, it covers every type. It works on a province.

label: Stationed men-at-arms damage (percent)
summary: Changes by a percentage the damage of all stationed men-at-arms in the province.
details: It uses the same display name as stationed_maa_damage_add. It works on a province.

label: Stationed men-at-arms damage per piety level
summary: Changes by a percentage the damage of all stationed men-at-arms in the province, for each piety level.
details: The game shows it as "Stationed Men-at-Arms Damage per piety level". Going by the name, whose piety level counts is not stated; the game documents nothing more. It works on a province.

label: Stationed men-at-arms pursuit
summary: Adds a flat amount of pursuit to all stationed men-at-arms in the province.
details: The game shows it as "Stationed Men-at-Arms Pursuit". Pursuit makes a victorious army turn more routed soldiers into dead ones after a battle. It works on a province.
